the effects of (+/-)- kavain on voltage-dependent Ca2+ and/or Na+ channel currents in cultured neonatal rat dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
the pharmacological activity of (+/-)-Kavain on voltage-dependent Na+ and Ca(2+) channels in cultured dorsal root neurons.
the pharmacological effects of kava pyrones on ion channels.

(+/-)- kava pyrones reduce voltage-activated Ca(2+)- and Na(+) currents in dorsal root ganglion neurons from neonatal rats.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(+/-)-Kavain has the ability to inhibit voltage-gated Ca2+ currents, but not voltage-gated Na+ currents, and that (+/-)- Kavain can inhibit both voltage-gated Na and Ca channels in the absence of a solvent, and only voltage-gated Na currents in the presence of a solvent.
(+/-)- kavain is a blocker of voltage-activated ion channels in dorsal root ganglion neurons from neonatal rats, which may be involved in the pharmacological action of kava pyrones.
(+/-)- kava pyrone reduces voltage-activated Na(+) and Ca(2+) currents in DRG neurons, which may be a basis for its muscle relaxing and anticonvulsive properties.

the effects of kava are not due to a single active compound, but rather a combination of several different compounds.
